## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

To start new - Cltr + Alt + I


# The Penguins

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# Install pacman once, then use it to install (if missing) and load the rest
if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, gapminder, gtsummary)
```

```{r}
# Load the Palmer Penguins dataset
pacman::p_load(palmerpenguins)
data(penguins)
head(penguins)
```

## First graph

```{r}
#| warning: false
# Scatter plot: flipper length vs body mass, colour = species, shape = island
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g,
                     colour = species, shape = island)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Adelie    = "#2a78d6",
                                 Chinstrap = "#eb6834",
                                 Gentoo    = "#1baf7a")) +
  labs(title = "Penguins with longer flippers are heavier",
       x = "Flipper length (mm)",
       y = "Body mass (g)",
       colour = "Species", shape = "Island") +
  theme_minimal()
```
